the standard video restoration order (denoise then unsharp — the classic detail-restoration chain; the A/B VLM gate froze anime=mild, 3d=strong)
render.implementation: (1) THE BOARD: VLM roster keyframes every 4 frames (17 keyframes) + the dedicated per-frame fine ball pass f050-f064 + an ANCHORED affine solve (posts-exact, np.linalg.lstsq 5-point re-fit residual 0.00px; the free-variant refused), outlier pass + PCHIP + MA(5), deterministic OpenCV render (mow-stripe pitch, penalty box, goal net box, numbered markers, ball trail, GOAL pulse) + ffmpeg x264 8fps. (2) THE CLARITY: fastNlMeansDenoisingColored(h=4) + unsharp(sigma 1.4, A/B VLM-gated amounts) on every propagated frame. (3) THE BALL: per-frame cut-and-paste f052-f064 — the anime's own ball disc (Hough circle-on-ball, vision-verified) cut from the stuck sites (annulus grass fill + pitch-line redraw, no TELEA), pasted along the inverse-affine flight that ends in the net.

designGate.method: the design gate by MEASUREMENT before freezing: flicker = mean abs consecutive-frame diff (grayscale 0-255, 64 pairs) before/after per kind with the no-regression bar at x1.05; the before baselines honestly attributed: three-d-game/anime-npr = the 70-C propagated flicker (the reprep3-equivalent state), tactical = the source clip's own band 17.5965 (the real-camera view the board replaces; the board's own static gate <= 1.0); the strict merged-crop ball-count; the six-question board check; the clarity edge-strength gain >= +15% with the A/B VLM gate; the five-question overall verdict
designGate.ballCheck: MAX: 1 (f054: '1'; f058: '1'; f062: '1') — merged-crop vision gate (vacated-site crop + flight-position crop side by side, 160x160 each) on the final frames
designGate.ballTrajectory: LEAVES the shooter at the strike and ends in the net — the VLM verdict verbatim: "The sequence shows the ball leaving the shooter's foot after the strike (visible in IMAGE2 and IMAGE3 as it travels toward the goal) and ultimately ending in the net, as confirmed by IMAGE4 where the ball is seen inside the goal and the goalkeeper has failed to stop it."
designGate.boardCheck: 6/6 (A YES: flat top-down 2D view of a soccer pitch; B YES: colored circular markers with numbers 1,4,5,7,9 on the field; C YES: red marker 9, blue marker 4 and the white ball all change positions across the three frames; D YES: goal with white net and yellow goalkeeper marker clearly visible on the right; E YES: in the last frame the white ball is inside the goal/net with a GOAL! overlay; F YES: matches a broadcast-style 2D tactical board / match-engine view) - one z-ai vision call on b010+b032+b058 together; verbatim verdict in board-check-raw.txt
